title: A Summit for the Current
premise: Lior Sandoval has spent a decade avoiding the river country where their mother, archaeologist Ines Sandoval, vanished during an expedition — and avoiding the truth that Ines may have chosen the dig over her child. When old rival Cass Merrow hires Lior's crew to recover Ines's final findings before monsoon floods and glacier calving seal the valley forever, Lior accepts for reasons they won't admit: the site holds answers about the night their mother disappeared. With a leaking boat, a taciturn local guide named Wren who knew Ines better than her own family did, and Cass's hidden agenda threatening everyone, Lior must choose between exposing the truth of what happened and protecting the loyalty of the crew who trust them. In the end, Lior opens Ines's sealed field journal, learns she died saving Wren's village from a flood her own excavation triggered, and chooses to publish the truth — inheriting not her secrets but her responsibility.
about_author: Sable Dunmore is the pen name of a former river guide turned writer who spent six seasons running glacial waterways in South America before trading rapids for manuscripts. Their fiction is known for landscapes that behave like characters and protagonists who would rather outrun their pasts than outswim them.

chapters.title: The Job That Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: POV: Lior. Running cargo runs on the coast, Lior is cornered by Cass Merrow with a contract to retrieve Ines Sandoval's final expedition records before the calving season closes the upper valley. Lior refuses, then finds Cass has already hired their crew — including loyal deckhand Tomas, who needs the payout. The beat: resentment curdling into reluctant commitment as Lior signs on to control the damage.

chapters.title: Monsoon Water Rising
chapters.summary: POV: Lior, with a midpoint shift to Wren. Upstream in worsening rain, the boat springs a leak and the crew shelters in a river village where guide Wren Halawi reveals she was on Ines's last expedition — and that Ines sent her away the night she died. Cass pushes the crew harder than safety allows. The beat: trust fraying; Lior realizes everyone on this boat is keeping a secret.

chapters.title: What the Glacier Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Lior. Racing the calving season, the crew reaches the sealed camp and finds Ines's strongbox — inside it, a journal proving the excavation dammed a meltwater channel that flooded Wren's village, and that Ines stayed behind diverting the flow. Cass wants the journal destroyed to protect the expedition's legacy fund. The beat: climax — Lior must choose inheritance as legacy or as truth while the glacier begins to calve.

chapters.title: A Summit for the Current
chapters.summary: POV: Lior, closing on Wren. As the ice gives way, Lior chooses Wren and the villagers' account over Cass's money, publishing the journal and dissolving the crew contract with full disclosure. On the run back downriver, Lior scatters Ines's ashes at the confluence she loved. The beat: resolution — grief answered by responsibility, and love chosen over duty without shame.
